newsitem.title: UK: World sugar consumption may rise 22 mln t by 2005.
newsitem.headline: World sugar consumption may rise 22 mln t by 2005.

text.p: World sugar consumption should grow by between 19 and 22 million tonnes by the year 2005, mainly in developing countries, the managing director of statistician F.O. Licht said on Friday.

Speaking at a two-day conference hosted by Agra Europe, Helmut Ahlfeld said it would be reasonable to expect an annual sugar consumption growth of around 1.7 percent, extrapolating on the experience of the recent past and assuming that the decline in east European consumption had halted.
This would point to a global sugar offtake of around 133 million tonnes in 2005, up 19 million from 1995.
In October, Licht forecast world sugar disappearance at 119.62 million tonnes raw value for 1996/97 (September/August).

But if a more positive approach were taken towards developments in the world economy, then as much as 136 million tonnes of sugar could be consumed by 2005, assuming a growth rate of 2.0 percent, Ahlfeld said.

Developing nations, especially in Asia, would account for the bulk of the growth. "On the whole, developing countries still register strong consumption growth as long as enough sugar is available - and this is not going to change in the next few years," he said.
"Asia, with its rapidly rising incomes, high rates of population growth and still relatively low per capita consumption figures, will account for the bulk of increased world consumption.
"Europe would see only modest growth," he added.

The global sugar industry would also face increasing competition from isoglucose and other alternative sweeteners. Ahlfeld said world consumption of high-intensity sweeteners could reach 13.3 million tonnes by 2005, up from 9.9 million in 1994, assuming that growth rates remained unchanged.
But he cautioned that the sector's rapid technological advances could easily accelerate the growth rate in consumption.
